CI/CD Integration

Integrate RoselineMCP into your continuous integration and deployment pipelines.

GitHub Actions

Code Quality Check

name: Code Quality

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  analyze:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    
    - name: Setup .NET
      uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
      with:
        dotnet-version: '9.0.x'
    
    - name: Install RoselineMCP
      run: |
        git clone https://github.com/phmatray/RoselineMCP.git
        cd RoselineMCP
        dotnet build -c Release
    
    - name: Analyze Solution
      run: |
        dotnet run --project RoselineMCP/RoselineMCP/RoselineMCP.csproj -- \
          analyzeSolution \
          --path ${{ github.workspace }}/YourSolution.sln \
          --severity error
    
    - name: Check for Errors
      run: |
        if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
          echo "Code analysis found errors"
          exit 1
        fi

Automated Fixes

name: Auto-fix Code Issues

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * 1'  # Weekly on Monday

jobs:
  fix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with:
        token: ${{ secrets.PAT }}  # Personal access token for pushing
    
    - name: Setup .NET
      uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
      with:
        dotnet-version: '9.0.x'
    
    - name: Run RoselineMCP Fixes
      run: |
        docker run --rm \
          -v ${{ github.workspace }}:/workspace \
          phmatray/roseline-mcp:latest \
          applyFixes \
          --project /workspace/YourProject.csproj \
          --ids CS0168,IDE0005,RCS1213
    
    - name: Create Pull Request
      uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@v5
      with:
        title: 'Auto-fix code issues'
        body: 'Automated fixes applied by RoselineMCP'
        branch: auto-fix/code-issues

Azure DevOps

Pipeline Task

trigger:
- main

pool:
  vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'

steps:
- task: UseDotNet@2
  inputs:
    packageType: 'sdk'
    version: '9.0.x'

- script: |
    docker pull phmatray/roseline-mcp:latest
  displayName: 'Pull RoselineMCP'

- script: |
    docker run --rm \
      -v $(Build.SourcesDirectory):/workspace:ro \
      phmatray/roseline-mcp:latest \
      analyzeSolution \
      --path /workspace/Solution.sln \
      --severity warning \
      > analysis-report.json
  displayName: 'Analyze Code'

- task: PublishBuildArtifacts@1
  inputs:
    pathToPublish: 'analysis-report.json'
    artifactName: 'CodeAnalysis'

GitLab CI

stages:
  - analysis
  - fix

analyze:
  stage: analysis
  image: mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:9.0
  script:
    - git clone https://github.com/phmatray/RoselineMCP.git
    - cd RoselineMCP && dotnet build -c Release
    - dotnet run --project RoselineMCP/RoselineMCP.csproj -- \
        analyzeSolution \
        --path $CI_PROJECT_DIR/Solution.sln \
        --exclude Test
  artifacts:
    reports:
      dotnet: analysis-report.json

apply-fixes:
  stage: fix
  image: phmatray/roseline-mcp:latest
  script:
    - applyFixes \
        --project $CI_PROJECT_DIR/Project.csproj \
        --ids CS0168,IDE0005 \
        --previewOnly
  only:
    - merge_requests

Jenkins

pipeline {
    agent any
    
    stages {
        stage('Checkout') {
            steps {
                checkout scm
            }
        }
        
        stage('Analysis') {
            steps {
                script {
                    docker.image('phmatray/roseline-mcp:latest').inside {
                        sh '''
                            analyzeSolution \
                              --path ${WORKSPACE}/Solution.sln \
                              --severity error \
                              > analysis.json
                        '''
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        
        stage('Report') {
            steps {
                publishHTML([
                    allowMissing: false,
                    alwaysLinkToLastBuild: true,
                    keepAll: true,
                    reportDir: '.',
                    reportFiles: 'analysis.json',
                    reportName: 'Code Analysis'
                ])
            }
        }
    }
    
    post {
        failure {
            emailext subject: 'Code Analysis Failed',
                     body: 'Check the analysis report',
                     to: 'team@example.com'
        }
    }
}

Quality Gates

Fail on Errors

#!/bin/bash
RESULT=$(analyzeSolution --path Solution.sln)
ERRORS=$(echo $RESULT | jq '.diagnosticSummary.error')

if [ "$ERRORS" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "Build failed: $ERRORS errors found"
    exit 1
fi

Warning Threshold

#!/bin/bash
MAX_WARNINGS=50
RESULT=$(analyzeSolution --path Solution.sln)
WARNINGS=$(echo $RESULT | jq '.diagnosticSummary.warning')

if [ "$WARNINGS" -gt "$MAX_WARNINGS" ]; then
    echo "Too many warnings: $WARNINGS (max: $MAX_WARNINGS)"
    exit 1
fi

Integration with SonarQube

# Export RoselineMCP results to SonarQube format
analyze_and_convert() {
    RESULT=$(analyzeSolution --path Solution.sln)
    
    # Convert to SonarQube generic issue format
    echo $RESULT | jq '{
        issues: .topDiagnostics | map({
            engineId: "RoselineMCP",
            ruleId: .id,
            severity: .severity | ascii_upcase,
            type: "CODE_SMELL",
            primaryLocation: {
                message: .message,
                filePath: .file,
                textRange: {
                    startLine: .line,
                    startColumn: .column
                }
            }
        })
    }' > sonar-report.json
    
    # Import to SonarQube
    sonar-scanner \
        -Dsonar.externalIssuesReportPaths=sonar-report.json
}

Notifications

Slack Integration

# Send analysis results to Slack
RESULT=$(analyzeSolution --path Solution.sln)
ERRORS=$(echo $RESULT | jq '.diagnosticSummary.error')
WARNINGS=$(echo $RESULT | jq '.diagnosticSummary.warning')

curl -X POST $SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{
    \"text\": \"Code Analysis Complete\",
    \"attachments\": [{
      \"color\": $([ $ERRORS -eq 0 ] && echo '\"good\"' || echo '\"danger\"'),
      \"fields\": [
        {\"title\": \"Errors\", \"value\": \"$ERRORS\", \"short\": true},
        {\"title\": \"Warnings\", \"value\": \"$WARNINGS\", \"short\": true}
      ]
    }]
  }"

Best Practices

  1. Run on Every PR: Catch issues before merge
  2. Set Quality Gates: Define acceptable thresholds
  3. Automate Fixes: Schedule regular cleanup
  4. Track Metrics: Monitor trends over time
  5. Integrate with Tools: Connect to existing workflows
